claim: The paper gives the first quantum algorithm for Lasso regression, running in O~(r*sqrt(mn)/epsilon + poly(n,1/epsilon)) time versus O~(mn^2 + n^3) classically (Corollary 26).
paper: Accelerating Regression Tasks with Quantum Algorithms (arXiv:2509.24757 / OpenReview TBSyYj4VV6)
method: Leverage-score sparsifier applied to Lasso (coordinate descent on full vs weighted sketch); m-scaling timed; asymptotic ordering symbolic.
reason: Sparsifier (1+/-eps) embedding holds (gram rel-err=0.113<=0.15); Lasso optimum on sketch within 0.50 of full (ratio=0.002). Classical Lasso/CD is O(m n^2+n^3): full solve slope=1.00, sketch slope=-0.67 in m. Quantum/classical -> 0. NOTE: 'first quantum Lasso algorithm' is a qualitative contribution claim (not computable); runtime ordering verified. EVIDENCE BOUNDARY: literal quantum construction (QRAM) NOT executed on CPU.

mutation.description: (M1) s<r/eps^2 breaks optimum-preservation; (M2) tighter eps needs more samples; (M3) quantum sqrt(m) required for speedup.
